review_type: independent full-path final implementation/code acceptance-readiness review
summary: The exact e4e4eab candidate has three code defects: delayed unscoped native cancellation can cancel a replacement attempt; the host calls a package error initializer that is not public and cannot compile; and explicit provider Remove retains the binding so a fresh Google login immediately restores the removed identity's account access. The latter was independently reproduced in temporary synthetic SQLite. Prior Apple relay/state/receipt fixes remain intact. Native finalization, account/session/action checks, recovery/collision, provider verification, logging, migration/cleanup, Mac password contracts, MCP coexistence and the ten browser-journey sources were inspected. Full feature/production acceptance is unavailable.

findings.title: Scope deferred cancellation to the attempt that was cancelled
findings.evidence_kind: static source interleaving; no physical-device reproduction
findings.description: authenticate captures an attempt id for result callbacks, but onCancel schedules a new MainActor Task calling unscoped cancel(). If A's cancellation task is queued and replacement B starts first, A's deferred handler clears B's active controller/browser and resumes B's continuation with CancellationError. An already-cancelled caller can also enter authenticate before an initial cancellation check. This is a coordinator-generation defect; no wrong-owner session installation or data loss was demonstrated.
reproducible_interleaving: Cancel A, enqueueing its MainActor cancellation task.
Start B before that task runs; active and continuation now belong to B.
Run A's queued task; unscoped cancel clears B.
findings.requirement: 023-FR-015/016 and native contract: cancellation/supersession must preserve the current attempt, owner and local work.
findings.recommendation: Check Task cancellation before replacing the current attempt; capture A's id and guard active?.id == id on MainActor before applying its deferred cancellation.

findings.title: Avoid calling an internal synthesized initializer from the iOS host
findings.evidence_kind: static Swift access-control proof; root separately reported actual Xcode CI failure
findings.description: The host invokes NativeAuthCallback.InvalidCallback(). InvalidCallback is a public struct without a public initializer, so its synthesized initializer is internal to BrainBuddyAPI and inaccessible from the iOS app module. This stops the native host build. I did not run Xcode here; the source is decisive and root reported the corresponding real CI diagnostic.
findings.recommendation: Throw the coordinator's existing local Failure for an absent callback URL, or otherwise use an accessible error; no public API expansion is necessary.

findings.title: Explicit Remove must prevent the removed provider from regaining login authority
findings.evidence_kind: independently exercised synthetic production-service reproduction at exact input SHA
findings.description: unlink changes the binding to disabled, revokes provider sessions/proofs, and retains the subject. Public provider completion treats that retained binding as the old account's identity and reactivates any nonactive state. After password-confirmed Remove Google, an independent brand-new Google callback/login returned signed_in to the same owner and changed the binding to active/generation2. Removing a compromised provider therefore does not remove its access to the BrainBuddy account. The retained personal linkage also never expires: metadata maintenance omits bindings and terminal Apple cleanup erases credential payloads only, contradicting the disconnection retention disclosure.
findings.reproduction_stdin:
from pathlib import Path
from tempfile import TemporaryDirectory
import pytest
from tests import conftest
from tests.test_modern_auth_service import make_modern, provider_handoff
from app.schemas.modern_auth import PasswordConfirmRequest, AccountActionRequest

with TemporaryDirectory(prefix='modern-auth-final-unlink-') as directory:
    data = Path(directory)/'data'
    data.mkdir()
    mp = pytest.MonkeyPatch()
    generator = conftest.container.__wrapped__(data, mp)
    container = next(generator)
    try:
        service, mail, sent, provider, clock = make_modern(container)
        owner = container.auth_service.seed_admin(email='new@gmail.com', password='synthetic-long-password')
        _, password_token, _ = container.auth_service.login(email=owner.email, password='synthetic-long-password')
        with service.store.transaction() as c:
            c.execute('INSERT INTO auth_identity_bindings(id,user_id,provider,issuer,namespace,subject,created_at,updated_at,email,email_verified) VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?,1)', ('google-binding',owner.id,'google','https://accounts.google.com','brainbuddy','subject-a',clock().isoformat(),clock().isoformat(),owner.email))
        recent = service.confirm_password(PasswordConfirmRequest(current_password='synthetic-long-password', expected_account_id=owner.id, action='unlink:google'),raw_token=password_token)
        service.unlink('google',AccountActionRequest(expected_account_id=owner.id,recent_proof=recent.recent_proof),raw_token=password_token)
        with service.store.connection() as c:
            print('repro_removed_google_retained_binding:',dict(c.execute('SELECT state,subject,generation FROM auth_identity_bindings').fetchone()))
        resumed = service.complete_provider(provider_handoff(service))
        print('repro_removed_google_still_signs_in:',resumed.payload.status, resumed.payload.user.id==owner.id)
        with service.store.connection() as c:
            print('repro_removed_google_reactivated:',dict(c.execute('SELECT state,generation FROM auth_identity_bindings').fetchone()))
    finally:
        try:
            next(generator)
        except StopIteration:
            pass
        mp.undo()
findings.requirement: 023-FR-005/006/007/018, approved D04 Remove consequences ('You won't be able to sign in with Google'), and removal of relevant bindings/personal metadata on unlink.
findings.recommendation: Distinguish signed provider revocation from explicit user unlink. Public fresh or previously staged provider proofs must not restore explicitly removed authority; require authenticated fresh link before it can regain the account. Erase Google linkage immediately and Apple linkage after only the bounded cleanup/active-lease necessity, preserving generation safety, retry and final purge. Invalidate or reject old provider attempts/handoffs, and test explicit relink plus stale/current cleanup races.
